> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4bb57ba2dd4129ddafc00eae9accd75910c42f8a` — the merge of head `d366c1712d1d9f3d979bbea5293e5870c7ebe5d1` into base `6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4bb57ba2dd4129ddafc00eae9accd75910c42f8a && git checkout 4bb57ba2dd4129ddafc00eae9accd75910c42f8a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91 d366c1712d1d9f3d979bbea5293e5870c7ebe5d1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91 && git merge --no-ff d366c1712d1d9f3d979bbea5293e5870c7ebe5d1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6b9e6df909dade0e2e2f2e4ee90de22fefff2a91` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #24821 · `domain:services` seat 2 · `os-support-ai` · `session_01UmqzD97e14iws6hmVhgZ5y` · 2026-10-20T12:36Z · head `d366c1712d`, first round, the review of record for claim `6289134908`.

1. **Form:**
   - The first line is `Fixes #24821`; the seat's grep of the body finds no other closing keyword beside an issue number.
   - `Clause-②: no` at line start in the body, in the changeset and in the claim. The seat confirmed it: the insert was refused before and is refused now, and both new members (`crossedByPlatformAdmin` on `computeLayeredRlsFilter`'s return, and `computeWriteTenantWall`) are `private` on `SecurityPlugin`. The package's `exports` map reaches only `.`, so nothing published moves.
   - One `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/plugin-security`.
   - 4 files, +478/−24. No `packages/objectql/**`, no `tenant-layer.ts`, no `packages/spec/**`, no new error code. One file sits outside the claim's surface (item 4).
   - Path face read with the files endpoint on this head: `check-governed-merges --pr 24868` reports 0 of 4 paths governed, 502 changed lines. Ordinary queue landing.
2. **Premise and fix:**
   - **Premise measured.** At base `4be728131` the pin alone was `4 failed | 12 passed`, under `group` and `isolated`, with `ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED` where `PERMISSION_DENIED` belongs. Every control was already green.
   - **The fix is one arm in step 3.7.** An insert from a caller whose `null` Layer 0 is a platform operator's crossing, from a session with no active organization, is judged on its stored image in the same `postHookWriteImageCheck` seam. It throws the same D2 refusal (`refuseNoActiveOrganization`) as the #24784 arm. It runs after the `beforeInsert` chain and before the engine's organization check, so a hook that places the row is still admitted.
   - **The crossing fact asks the one ladder, it doesn't copy it.** `crossedByPlatformAdmin` re-asks `computeTenantLayer0Verdict` with only `isPlatformAdmin` withheld. The seat read the ladder in `packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts`. `single`, tenancy disabled and a missing `organization_id` column all answer `none` before the exemption rung, so they answer `none` both ways and can never count as a crossing. The changeset's "every `single` answer is unchanged" therefore follows from the ladder's order, not from a pin. The cost is a second call of a pure function on the write path.
   - **Pins and ablation.** A new real-stack file (ObjectQL + SqlDriver + SecurityPlugin), one block per walled posture: the refusal, single and bulk, compared whole with the member's answer on the same object; six unchanged neighbours. Two ablation legs were each red as predicted and restored to the HEAD blob:
     - A1, the arm off: `5 failed`, the four refusals plus the unit refusal.
     - A2, the crossing discriminator off: `2 failed`, the opted-out-of-tenancy control under both postures.
3. **Gates:**
   - CI on `d366c1712d`, read by the seat after the last shard completed: 41 check-runs, 34 success, 7 skipped, 0 failed. Every skip is on the roster in `scripts/pm/check-expected-skips.mjs`, read from the file because the shared checkout has no `yaml` package to run it: Build Docs, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix, Packed-tarball smoke, and the 18.x upgrade harness.
   - Local: 69 derived, 69 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. Two prerequisite exits (3) were re-measured after a workspace build.
   - Package suite: `plugin-security` 196 files, 4066 passed and 45 skipped; typecheck exit 0.
   - Docs drift (`6290453151`): the six named pages reach this change through the class name or the private `computeLayeredRlsFilter`. The seat's grep of `content/docs/permissions` finds no page that says an operator's organization-less insert is admitted, so no page is now false. `content/docs/releases/` is untouched.
4. **Accepted deviations:**
   - **`no-active-organization-write-refusal.test.ts` (+55/−11) is outside the claim's surface.** Its control "a true PLATFORM operator crosses the wall on a posture-permitting object" pinned exactly the branch this card changes: an organization-less insert passing the middleware, which on the real stack answered 500. Leaving it would have pinned the defect. The re-judged pins keep the crossing measured on what it really admits (the operator's update with no active organization) and keep the business-object sibling's posture scoping. Same package; declared in the PR body.
   - **The answer follows ADR-0131 D9 where ADR-0123 D2's scope paragraph says otherwise.** D2 exempts "a platform operator crossing the wall by ADR-0095 D3", and its Consequences list platform operators under "What does not change". D9 refuses this write anyway, so the outcome (refused, nothing stored) is unchanged and only the answer moves from the 500 to the D2 403. The PR changes no ADR text (`docs/adr/**` is Tier H). The amendment belongs to #24823 (item 5).
5. **Out of scope** (the PR's `## Acceptance notes`, one line each):
   - Note 1, ADR-0123 D2's scope sentence: carrier #24823, the open amendment card. The seat posts the pointer there at landing.
   - Note 2, the operator's cross-organization by-id update answers 404 while the same caller reads the row: Acceptance notes. It was measured in-process only. No public door was measured and no real producer is named, and only the top rung reaches it.
   - Note 3, populations the engine's organization check may still answer 500 for a non-system caller: Acceptance notes. All four are unmeasured; this is the card's `domain:engine` candidate.
   - Note 4, `canWriteObject`'s row-less create preview still answers `true` for this operator: Acceptance notes, the same boundary #24784 recorded.
6. **Landing:** ordinary queue landing. Every check on this head is green or an expected skip, so the seat flips it (`pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`) on this record.
